t: Time to Cross a Bridge — Event Simulation with Priority Queues
o: We restate: k workers shuttle n boxes across a bridge; each worker i takes right_i to cross rightward, pick_i to pick, left_i to cross back, put_i to put down. Only one worker is on the bridge at a time, and when the bridge frees up, waiting box-carrying workers on the right cross first (least efficient first, ties by larger index), otherwise waiting workers on the left cross (same priority rule). We must report when the last box arrives on the left bank (after crossing, not after putting down). Example 1: worker 2 crosses (1), picks (1), crosses back finishing at 6 — answer 6. Example 2 shows we stop counting after the final crossing. Constraints (n,k ≤ 1e4, times ≤ 1000) mean we can simulate every crossing event: at most ~2n+k events, each handled in O(log k) with heaps.
k: Simulate the process chronologically; whenever nobody can act, jump time forward to the next 'worker becomes free' event.
Priority = maximize left_i+right_i, tie-break by larger index; keep two waiting heaps (left/right bank) and two 'busy-until' heaps.
The answer is the completion time of the n-th right-to-left crossing.

a.i: Keep min-heaps of 'busy until time t' workers for picking (right bank) and putting (left bank), and max-heaps keyed by (left+right, index) for workers waiting on each bank. At each moment, release every worker whose busy time has passed, then act: if someone waits on the right they cross left (finishing a box); else if boxes remain, someone crosses right. If no one can act, jump cur to the earliest future release time.
s: Initialize the left-waiting heap with all k workers, cur=0, remaining=n.
Loop while boxes remain or workers are still on the right/picking: release due workers from busy heaps into waiting heaps.

If right-waiting nonempty: pop best, cur+=left_i, decrement remaining, update answer, schedule put-down at cur+put_i. Else if boxes remain and left-waiting nonempty: pop best, cur+=right_i, schedule pick at cur+pick_i.
Otherwise jump cur to the minimum relevant busy time.

c.python:
import heapq
class Solution:
    def findCrossingTime(self, n: int, k: int, time: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        wl = [(-(time[i][0] + time[i][2]), -i) for i in range(k)]
        heapq.heapify(wl)
        wr, bl, br = [], [], []
        cur, rem, ans = 0, n, 0
        while rem > 0 or wr or br:
            while bl and bl[0][0] <= cur:
                _, i = heapq.heappop(bl)
                heapq.heappush(wl, (-(time[i][0] + time[i][2]), -i))
            while br and br[0][0] <= cur:
                _, i = heapq.heappop(br)
                heapq.heappush(wr, (-(time[i][0] + time[i][2]), -i))
            if wr:
                _, ni = heapq.heappop(wr)
                i = -ni
                cur += time[i][2]
                rem -= 1
                ans = max(ans, cur)
                heapq.heappush(bl, (cur + time[i][3], i))
            elif rem > 0 and wl:
                _, ni = heapq.heappop(wl)
                i = -ni
                cur += time[i][0]
                heapq.heappush(br, (cur + time[i][1], i))
            else:
                nxt = float('inf')
                if br: nxt = br[0][0]
                if rem > 0 and bl: nxt = min(nxt, bl[0][0])
                cur = nxt
        return ans

a.t: O((n + k) log k) — each worker enters/leaves heaps a constant number of times per box cycle
a.sp: O(n + k) — heaps hold at most all workers plus pending events

w: Use the heap simulation in an interview — it directly mirrors the rules. Pitfalls: forgetting that the answer excludes the final put-down; forgetting that once all n boxes are dispatched no more left-bank crossings happen; mishandling the tie-break (larger index = less efficient). A common follow-up: what if multiple bridges existed (answer: one queue per bridge).
